summary: Mobile QA pass for Phase 39M.4: readability sweep, station artwork on Home, new /stations browser, and Games polish. 3 of 4 tasks PASS. Readability sweep is 95% clean but TWO regressions remain: (1) Passport screen 'City Leaderboard' CTA text is white on an amber-6% tinted (effectively white) row -> invisible. (2) Play & Win 'LOSE' history badge is white text on white card bg -> invisible (only the WIN case overrides the tag bg to green). All other requested screens (Home, Wallet, Games, More, News, Leaderboard, Notifications, Coupons, Play & Win *headers*, Commute, Trivia picker, Lobbies, Onboarding, Offer/Coupons list) render dark slate text on light bg with no white-on-light offenders. Station artwork on Home now shows real cover images (VIP Lounge / Premium Mehfil / DFW Bollywood). /stations end-to-end works: 88 imported stations load with favicons + FLAGSHIP badges + country/language subtitles; search 'bollywood' narrows total to 41; language chip 'hindi' broadens total to 2,012; tapping a row starts playback (POST /api/radio/play/{id}) and the persistent MiniPlayer appears with station name, subtitle and pause icon. Home 'home-all-stations-cta' and Channels 'channels-all-stations-cta' both navigate to /stations. Games tab section headings render at 12px weight 800 slate-600 (enlarged/darkened vs old 10px muted style) and each quick-game row shows label (14px slate-900) + description line (10px slate-400): Spin & Win / Music Trivia / Guess the Lyric all show correct descriptions.

ui_bugs.issue: 'City Leaderboard' CTA text is color '#fff' on a parent card whose backgroundColor is rgba(255,215,0,0.06) — effectively white on white, so the label is INVISIBLE. Only the trophy icon and the sub-line 'See top ambassadors in your city' are legible. Reference: /app/mobile/app/(tabs)/passport.tsx:399  ->  leaderCta: { color: '#fff', ... }. Fix: use COLORS.gold or COLORS.text (or give the row a solid amber fill if the white text is intentional).

In Played history rows the LOSE badge renders white text on a white card. The style is resultTag: { backgroundColor: COLORS.card } (which is #ffffff) and resultTagText: { color: '#fff' }. The WIN case overrides the bg to COLORS.green so WIN badges are visible, but the LOSE fallback keeps the white card bg — result: two INVISIBLE 'LOSE' pills in the history list. Reference: /app/mobile/app/play-and-win.tsx:215-216. Fix: give the lose branch a colored bg (e.g. COLORS.red or slate-200) OR set resultTagText.color to COLORS.text and only flip to '#fff' when a colored bg is applied.

issues: No 'Skip' affordance found on the visible onboarding step — only BACK / CONTINUE. Task item said 'Onboarding is skippable'; if that refers to a Skip button, it is currently missing. Text itself is readable (0 white-on-light offenders).

readability_sweep.method: Walked the DOM on each screen after login; flagged text elements with color >= rgb(235,235,235) whose nearest ancestor with a solid backgroundColor summed to >= 550 (i.e. near-white). Ignored elements sitting on a backgroundImage/gradient (avatars, hero art) since gradient fills can't be inspected via computed style.

action_items: FIX passport.tsx:399 leaderCta color '#fff' -> change to COLORS.gold or COLORS.text (or give the row a solid amber fill). Currently 'City Leaderboard' label is invisible.

FIX play-and-win.tsx:215-216 LOSE badge: either give the non-win branch a colored backgroundColor (e.g. COLORS.red / slate-200) or change resultTagText.color to COLORS.text with a conditional flip to '#fff' only when a colored bg is applied. LOSE badges are currently invisible white-on-white.
REVIEW onboarding.tsx: task list mentioned 'Onboarding is skippable' but no Skip button exists on the visible step (only BACK / CONTINUE). Confirm whether a Skip affordance is expected.
OPTIONAL (carryover from iter 30): migrate 'shadow*' props to 'boxShadow' and 'props.pointerEvents' to 'style.pointerEvents' to silence RN Web console warnings.
critical_code_review_comments: stations.tsx: clean singleton flow — releaseCurrent() before creating a new expo-audio player, setSession(null) so Radio screen's segment logic stays dormant on direct-stream stations, registerPlayer + audioController + updateNowPlaying all invoked so MiniPlayer/lockscreen state stays in sync.
stations.tsx: PAGE_SIZE=30 pagination + onEndReached loadMore + 400ms debounced search look correct; empty & failed states have distinct icon/title/copy.

The two remaining readability regressions have the same root cause pattern the sweep missed: hardcoded color:'#fff' on Text that ISN'T sitting on a colored button/gradient — the parent has either an amber-6% tint (passport) or COLORS.card=#ffffff (play-and-win LOSE). A grep for `color: '#fff'` in /app/mobile/app/**/*.tsx would surface the last remaining offenders quickly.

success_rate.frontend: 90% (12/14 requested screens clean; 2 residual white-on-light regressions)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase 39M.4 verification: Station artwork on Home + /stations screen (browse/search/play + MiniPlayer wiring) + Games polish are all working. Two readability regressions still remain and are the only blockers: (a) passport.tsx:399 leaderCta color='#fff' (invisible City Leaderboard CTA), (b) play-and-win.tsx:215-216 LOSE badge white-on-white. Both are 1-line style fixes. After fixes, re-run just those two screens plus a quick grep for any remaining `color: '#fff'` on Text outside of buttons/avatars/active chips/badges/dark screens.
rca of the issue: The Phase 39M.4 sweep converted title/name/label/value/input/prompt style keys to COLORS.text but preserved '#fff' on any element the author judged to be sitting on a colored button, avatar, active chip, badge, or dark screen. Two elements were misclassified: (1) passport.leaderCta LOOKS like a badge-style CTA but its parent row uses a very faint amber tint (alpha 0.06) which resolves to near-white when composited over the slate-50 screen bg. (2) play-and-win.resultTag defaults to backgroundColor: COLORS.card (#ffffff) and only the WIN branch overrides it to green; the LOSE branch inherits white bg while the text color stays '#fff'. Both are pure style fixes with no functional change required.
